title: On-call & Incident Response Guidelines and Runbooks
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview:

This document defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response practices, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and recommended customer / status-page communication templates. It is intended for all engineers and SREs who participate in on-call rotations or are responsible for incident handling.

Scope:
- Applies to all production-facing services managed by the Redwood serving and control-plane teams (hosted API, routing, quota, and observability subsystems).
- Includes detection, triage, mitigation, escalation, communication, postmortem, and follow-up actions.

Goals and Principles:
- Restore service to acceptable levels as quickly and safely as possible.
- Communicate clearly to internal stakeholders and affected customers.
- Capture root cause and remediate to prevent recurrence.
- Respect on-callers: reasonable shift length, handoffs, and interruption budgets.

Key SLOs and thresholds (reference):
- Platform availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted inference control plane.
- Inference tail latency (P99): <= 300 ms for typical small models under normal load.
- Error budget burn policy: >50% monthly burn triggers stakeholder notification; >75% triggers mitigation plan.
- Pager thresholds:
  - P0: Full-region outage or control-plane unavailability affecting >10% of paid requests.
  - P1: Major degradation (>=50% increase in P99 latency or error rate >1% sustained for 5 min).
  - P2: Partial degradation affecting a single region or non-critical tenants.

Roles and Responsibilities:
- Primary on-call (Responder): First to acknowledge and drive incident until triage or handoff.
- Secondary on-call (Escalation): Backstop for unresolved P1/P0 incidents; provides deeper troubleshooting.
- Incident Commander (IC): For P0/P1 incidents, the IC coordinates cross-team work, communications, and escalation. IC is usually assigned by the SRE lead or rotates among senior SREs.
- Communications Lead: Owns status updates to internal stakeholders and the public status page.
- Postmortem Lead: Owns postmortem write-up and action tracking.

On-call Rotation Policy:
- Rotation length: 1 week (Mon 00:00 UTC - Sun 23:59 UTC) for primary on-call.
- Secondary on-call: 2-week rotations (overlapping to maintain continuity).
- Shift coverage: 24/7 with primary + secondary present.
- Paging window: Primary gets all pages in rotation window unless explicitly swapped.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack + PagerDuty):
  1) Confirm last incident state and any ongoing mitigations.
  2) Share relevant runbook links and short list of active alerts.
  3) Confirm contact information and escalation path.
  4) Update oncall roster wiki with any expected unavailability.
- Swap and backup: If a scheduled on-caller is unavailable, they must swap at least 48 hours in advance and update the roster. Emergency swaps are permitted with manager approval.

Pager Escalation Matrix (example):
- Primary on-call: page -> 15 minutes to acknowledge -> if no ack, escalate to Secondary.
- Secondary: 10 minutes to acknowledge -> if no ack, escalate to IC rotation.
- IC rotation: 5 minutes to respond -> if no response, page Director on-call.

Incident Lifecycle (step-by-step):
1) Detection
   - Alerts from monitoring, customer reports, or status page triggers.
   - Triage starts immediately on pager ack.
2) Triage (first 10 minutes)
   - Confirm scope, impact, affected services, and initial severity.
   - Run quick checks: service health, retrospection of recent deploys, infra changes, regulation of traffic.
   - If P1/P0, assign IC and Communications Lead.
3) Mitigation (first 30-60 minutes)
   - Apply runbook playbooks for known failure modes.
   - If no runbook applies, follow safe rollback / traffic diversion steps.
   - Keep internal incident channel updated every 15 minutes for P1/P0.
4) Recovery and validation
   - Confirm metrics and customer reports show restored service.
   - Monitor for recurrence for at least 60 minutes after apparent recovery.
5) Postmortem and follow-up
   - Postmortem created within 3 business days (initial draft).
   - Publish postmortem and list action items with owners within 7 business days.
   - Close incident after all high-priority action items are scheduled.

Runbook Examples (copyable commands and checks):
- Service health quick checks:
  - kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving | grep -E "CrashLoopBackOff|Error"
  - curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.example.com/health || echo "health check failed"
  - jq '.errors | length' <(curl -sS https://api.redwood.example.com/metrics/errors)

- Cache / KV service restart (example):
  1) Reduce traffic to affected cluster: /ops/traffic-diverter --cluster serving-eu --scale-down 50
  2) Restart statefulset with zero-downtime pattern:
     kubectl rollout restart statefulset/kv-store -n infra || kubectl scale statefulset/kv-store --replicas=0 -n infra && kubectl scale statefulset/kv-store --replicas=3 -n infra

- Temporary mitigation pattern (traffic reroute):
  - Update routing rule to fallback model variant:
    curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/route/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","policy":"fallback","target":"model-x-small"}' || echo "route update failed"

Escalation and Communication Guidelines:
- Internal updates: every 15 minutes for P0/P1 until mitigation in place. Use dedicated incident Slack channel (#incident-<id>).
- Status page updates: short factual messages, no speculation. See templates below.
- Customer comms: For customers with active incidents, account teams will send targeted emails for P1/P0 within 30 minutes of severity assignment. Use templated language and include an incident link.

Status Page and Customer Communication Templates (copy and paste):
- Initial status page message (short):
  Title: Partial outage affecting inference requests in eu-west-1
  Body: We are investigating increased error rates for inference requests in eu-west-1. Some customers may experience failed or delayed requests. We will post updates every 15 minutes.

- Customer email (initial):
  Subject: Incident: Degraded inference performance in eu-west-1
  Hi <CustomerName>,

  We are investigating an issue impacting inference requests in eu-west-1. Our engineering teams are actively triaging. We will provide updates within 30 minutes. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with root cause and remediation when available.

  - On-call team, Redwood Inference Support

- Update example (status page):
  Update 1 (15 mins): Identified an upstream KV-store performance regression; rolling a targeted restart and routing ~30% of traffic to fallback cluster. Customers may see improved performance; next update in 15 minutes.

- Resolution message (status page):
  Resolved: The KV-store regression has been mitigated and traffic has been restored to normal routing. We are monitoring and will publish a root cause analysis soon.

Postmortem Template (required fields):
- Title: Short descriptive incident title
- Severity: P0/P1/P2
- Incident timeline (timestamped events)
- Summary (one-paragraph impact summary)
- Root cause: concise statement
- Detection and response: what alerted us and timeline of actions
- Impact: customers, internal systems, duration, metrics (error budget burn)
- Remediation and short-term mitigations performed
- Long-term fixes and owners (each action must have owner + ETA)
- Lessons learned and prevention plan
- Follow-up review date

Postmortem expectations and SLAs:
- Draft posted within 72 hours.
- Final postmortem with actions and owners within 7 business days.
- All critical actions (P0/P1) must have owners and due dates; tracked in engineering board.

Game Days and Exercises:
- Purpose: validate runbooks, testrestore procedures, and train on-call responders.
- Frequency: quarterly cross-team game days; SRE-run annual full-scale disaster exercise.
- Typical scenario: region failover, control-plane degraded, sudden capacity spike.
- Success criteria: recovery within SLO for at least 80% of simulated traffic and clear, documented runbook gaps identified.

Runbook Maintenance:
- Owners are responsible to review their service runbooks quarterly.
- When a runbook is updated, add a summary line to the runbook header and notify oncall roster.

Common Runbook Sections (each runbook should include):
- Scope and impact indicators
- Quick checks and dashboards to consult
- Safe mitigations and commands (with example CLI)
- Escalation points and contacts
- Post-incident next steps and rollback criteria

Service-specific example (Inference API front-end):
- Health checks:
  - curl -f https://api.redwood.example.com/health || (alert)
- If errors spike (>1% error rate sustained 5 min):
  1) Check recent deploys: git log -n 1 --pretty=oneline deploys/service/inference
  2) Scale up front-end pool: /ops/scale-service inference-frontend --replicas +2
  3) If scaling fails, enable degraded routing: /ops/traffic-diverter --route /v1/generate --policy degraded

On-call Etiquette and Wellbeing:
- Respect night-time quiet hours for non-urgent issues. For P2 incidents, prefer asynchronous updates unless escalation is necessary.
- Encourage blameless language in postmortems. Focus on system fixes and process changes.

Ownership and Contacts:
- On-call rotations owner: eng-sre team (sre-rotations@redwood.example.com)
- Incident commander rotation: eng-sre leads (page via PagerDuty)
- Status page owner: platform-ops@redwood.example.com
